TALK_REPLY_PRAISE_NEG_1: “Praise? After the games I've had? I'd rather you were straight with me.”
TALK_REPLY_PRAISE_NEG_2: He looks puzzled. “Are we watching the same matches?”

TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_POS_1: “Fair enough. I needed to hear that.”
TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_NEU_1: He listens without a word and leaves the office.
TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_NEU_2: “Everyone has bad spells. I'll get through it.”
TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_NEG_0: “That's not fair at all. I've given everything for this club.”
TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_NEG_1: He storms out. “Find someone else to blame.”
TALK_REPLY_CRITICISE_NEG_2: “If that's what you think of me, maybe I'm in the wrong place.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_POS_0: “Thanks for explaining. I know what I need to do to get in the side.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_POS_1: “That's honest. I can live with that for now.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_POS_2: “Good to know where I stand. I'll be ready when you need me.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEU_0: “I hear you. I just want to play.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEU_1: “Okay. Let's see how the next few weeks go.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEU_2: He shrugs. “It is what it is.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEG_0: “I'm not here to sit on the bench. I expected more.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEG_1: “That's not what I was told when I signed.”
TALK_REPLY_PLAYING_TIME_NEG_2: “So I'm just a squad player to you? Great.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_PLAYING_TIME_POS_0: “That's all I wanted to hear. I won't let you down.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_PLAYING_TIME_POS_1: “Deal. I'll be ready from the first minute.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_PLAYING_TIME_NEU_0: “Words are one thing. I'll believe it when I see my name on the team sheet.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_PLAYING_TIME_NEG_0: “I've heard that before. Forgive me if I don't get excited.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_POS_0: “Brilliant. I want my future to be here.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_POS_1: “Thank you. My agent will be glad to hear it.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_NEU_0: “Let's see what the offer looks like.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_NEU_1: “Fine. But don't leave it too late.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_NEG_0: “You've said things like that before. I'll wait for the paperwork.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_CONTRACT_NEG_1: “We'll see. I'm keeping my options open.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_SIGNING_POS_0: “That's the ambition I wanted to see. Let's go for it.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_SIGNING_POS_1: “Great. With a couple of quality players we can do something special.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_SIGNING_NEU_1: “Okay. I'll keep an eye on the news.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_SIGNING_NEG_0: “The board will never spend that kind of money. I'm not naive.”
TALK_REPLY_PROMISE_SIGNING_NEG_1: “I'll believe it when they're standing in the dressing room.”
TALK_REPLY_PATIENCE_POS_0: “Alright. I trust you. I'll keep working and wait for my chance.”
TALK_REPLY_PATIENCE_POS_1: “Okay, boss. I'll give it some time.”
TALK_REPLY_PATIENCE_NEU_0: “I can wait a little. Not forever.”
TALK_REPLY_PATIENCE_NEU_1: “Fine. But something has to change soon.”
TALK_REPLY_PATIENCE_NEG_1: “Patience? My career isn't going to wait for me.”
TALK_REPLY_REASSURE_POS_0: “Good. This is where I want to be.”
TALK_REPLY_REASSURE_POS_1: “Thanks for backing me. That settles it for me.”
TALK_REPLY_REASSURE_NEU_1: “I appreciate it. My head is all over the place right now.”
TALK_REPLY_REASSURE_NEG_0: “So you'll stand in the way of the move of my life?”
TALK_REPLY_REASSURE_NEG_1: “That's easy for you to say. It's my career.”
TALK_REPLY_OPEN_TO_OFFERS_POS_0: “Thanks for being honest with me. I respect that.”
TALK_REPLY_OPEN_TO_OFFERS_POS_1: “Good. If the right club comes in, I'd like to hear about it.”
TALK_REPLY_OPEN_TO_OFFERS_NEU_1: “Fair enough. I'll just focus on playing.”
TALK_REPLY_OPEN_TO_OFFERS_NEG_0: “So you want rid of me? After everything?”
TALK_REPLY_OPEN_TO_OFFERS_NEG_1: “I thought I mattered here. Apparently not.”
TALK_REPLY_ACCEPT_TRANSFER_POS_0: “Thank you. I'll give everything until the day I leave.”
TALK_REPLY_ACCEPT_TRANSFER_POS_1: “I appreciate you not standing in my way.”
TALK_REPLY_REFUSE_TRANSFER_POS_0: “Okay. I don't agree, but I'll keep giving my best.”
TALK_REPLY_REFUSE_TRANSFER_POS_1: “Fine. I'm a professional. You'll get nothing less from me.”
TALK_REPLY_REFUSE_TRANSFER_NEU_1: “That's your decision. Don't expect me to be happy about it.”
TALK_REPLY_REFUSE_TRANSFER_NEG_0: “Then you'll have an unhappy player on your hands.”

GLOSSARY_CONTINUE_DEF: Moves the calendar forward to the next thing that involves your club, usually your next match. The world keeps playing in the meantime.
GLOSSARY_OBJECTIVE_DEF: What the board wants from the season, from avoiding relegation to winning the league. It follows the club's means, mostly the wage bill compared with its rivals.
GLOSSARY_CONFIDENCE_DEF: How much the board trusts you, from 0 to 100. Results better than expected raise it, poor runs lower it; very low confidence can cost you the job.
GLOSSARY_REPUTATION_DEF: How well known and respected a club or a manager is. It affects which players are willing to join and which jobs you are offered.
GLOSSARY_OVERALL_DEF: A single number summing up a player's current ability in his position. For players outside your club it is your scouts' estimate.
GLOSSARY_POTENTIAL_DEF: The level a player could reach with good training and enough playing time. It is an estimate, and young players can surprise either way.
GLOSSARY_CONDITION_DEF: How fresh a player is. Matches and hard training lower it, rest restores it; tired players perform worse and get injured more often.
GLOSSARY_SHARPNESS_DEF: Readiness that only comes from playing. Players back from injury or out of the team need minutes, for example in friendlies, before they are at their best.
GLOSSARY_MORALE_DEF: A player's mood. Results, playing time, promises kept or broken and conversations with you all move it, and happy players play better.
GLOSSARY_FORM_DEF: Recent results or performances, shown as the last few matches: W for a win, D for a draw, L for a defeat.
GLOSSARY_FAMILIARITY_DEF: How well the squad knows your system. It grows with training and matches, and big changes of shape cost some of it for a while.
GLOSSARY_KNOWLEDGE_DEF: How much your scouts know about a player or a league. With little knowledge attributes are shown as ranges that narrow as the scouts keep watching.
GLOSSARY_TRANSFER_BUDGET_DEF: Money the board lets you spend on transfer fees. Sales add to it; it never allows the club to run out of cash.
GLOSSARY_WAGE_BUDGET_DEF: The most the club will pay its players each week. New contracts and renewals have to fit within it.
GLOSSARY_RELEASE_CLAUSE_DEF: A fee written into a contract: any club that offers it may talk to the player without his club's consent.
GLOSSARY_SELL_ON_DEF: A share of the next transfer fee that goes to the selling club when the player moves on again.
GLOSSARY_LOAN_DEF: A player joins another club for a set period and then returns. Loans give young players minutes and let clubs fill gaps cheaply.
GLOSSARY_FREE_AGENT_DEF: A player without a club. He can sign at any time and no transfer fee is due, only wages and a signing bonus.
GLOSSARY_TRANSFER_WINDOW_DEF: The periods, in summer and in winter, when clubs may register players bought from other clubs. Free agents can sign outside them.
GLOSSARY_SQUAD_STATUS_DEF: The role a player expects, from key player to backup. Playing him less than his status promises hurts his morale.
GLOSSARY_DELEGATION_DEF: Handing routine duties to your staff. Delegated work is done for you every day; anything you change by hand comes back to you.
GLOSSARY_PRESSING_DEF: How quickly and how high the team closes down the opponent with the ball. More pressing wins the ball back sooner but tires players faster.
GLOSSARY_XG_DEF: The chance that a shot becomes a goal, judged from where and how it was taken. Added over a match it shows who created the better chances.
GLOSSARY_SET_PIECES_DEF: Corners, free kicks, throw-ins and penalties. You choose the takers; good routines are a steady source of goals.
GLOSSARY_SHOUTS_DEF: Short instructions during a match, such as pushing higher or keeping the ball. Their effect fades over a few minutes.
GLOSSARY_YOUTH_INTAKE_DEF: The yearly group of teenagers joining your academy. Their quality depends on the academy's facilities, coaching and recruitment.
GLOSSARY_INTERNATIONAL_BREAK_DEF: Days when national teams play and club football stops. Called-up players leave for their country and may come back tired or injured.
GLOSSARY_PROMOTION_DEF: At the end of the season the top clubs of a division move up and the bottom clubs move down. Coloured zones in the table mark the places.
GLOSSARY_GOAL_DIFFERENCE_DEF: Goals scored minus goals conceded. It separates clubs level on points in the table.
GLOSSARY_EXTRA_TIME_DEF: A knockout tie still level after normal time goes to two extra halves of fifteen minutes, then to a penalty shootout.

ROLE_STANDARD_HELP: Plays the position the way the team has drilled it, with no special bias either way.
ROLE_LINE_KEEPER_HELP: Stays close to his goal line and leaves balls in behind to his defenders. Safer against lobs, but the back line cannot push as high.
ROLE_SWEEPER_KEEPER_HELP: Starts well off his line and races out to balls played in behind, so the defence can hold a high line. Needs pace and calm feet.
ROLE_INSIDE_FULL_BACK_HELP: When his side has the ball he leaves the touchline and steps into midfield to add a passer in the middle. He rarely overlaps.
ROLE_STOPPER_HELP: Steps out of the line to meet his man early and closes down quickly. Wins the ball high, but can leave space behind him.
ROLE_COVER_DEFENDER_HELP: Drops a few metres behind his partner to sweep up through balls and runners. Rarely steps out to press.
ROLE_ANCHOR_HELP: Sits in front of the back line in both phases, keeps passes simple and almost never joins attacks or shoots.
ROLE_PLAYMAKER_HELP: Drops in to receive and looks for the riskier forward pass. Team-mates seek him out; he leaves the runs to others.
ROLE_BOX_TO_BOX_HELP: Covers ground in both directions: presses, then arrives late in the box. Needs a big engine.
ROLE_SECOND_STRIKER_HELP: Plays just behind the striker and keeps running beyond him into the box, ready to shoot when the chance comes.
ROLE_INSIDE_FORWARD_HELP: Starts wide, then cuts inside onto his stronger side to shoot or combine. Leaves the flank to the full-back.
ROLE_TOUCHLINE_WINGER_HELP: Holds the width close to the line, takes his man on outside and crosses from the byline rather than shooting.
ROLE_TARGET_FORWARD_HELP: A fixed reference point up front: team-mates play forward passes into him and he holds the ball up instead of running in behind.
ROLE_POACHER_HELP: Lives on the shoulder of the last defender and gambles on chances in the box. Shoots early, presses little.
ROLE_PRESSING_FORWARD_HELP: The first defender: hunts the ball high up the pitch and sets off the press as soon as the opponents have it.
ROLE_FALSE_NINE_HELP: Drops off the defensive line into midfield to link play and drag centre-backs out of position. Rarely the one who runs in behind.
